title: Dates of the photos and Rappolo's Albert-system clarinet
summary: Russell asks dates; Mares dates Paul's picture to 1919 Chicago, and says Rappolo played a 13-key Albert system wooden clarinet. More photos of Fountain, Hogg, Boyd, Pecora.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: If there's anything of particular interest about these pictures, if you remember the dates of any of them, like we know the one down below the New Orleans Rhythm Kings, but Paul's, if you remember about the date?

Paul's was taken in 1919 in Chicago. The picture of George is probably 10 years old, probably goes back to 50. I took that picture myself. The picture of Rapp up here goes all the way back to the early 20s, probably 1920.
Does that show much of his clarinet? Can you see much about it? How many keys of it has that?
Yeah, that's the old Albert system. It's the Albert, of course. And a wooden clarinet. Right above Rapp, we have young Pete Fountain.
You almost read the label, the make on there, the brand, but I guess we can't see it.

Like I said, right above Rapp, we've got Pete Fountain. And Almond Hogg right next to him. Under Almond is Raymond Boyk, another one of the true greats of New Orleans, Dixieland. And to the right of Raymond, we have Santo Pacora, another real great.
